parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs national entry exposure (document-discrepancy refusals, possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility finding, X-markers halted, transit advisories against this country) with a division that criminalises gender-expressive performance (upheld misdemeanour, felony on repeat), mandates birth-sex facilities and prison/shelter placement, and supplies no statewide non-discrimination or gender-identity hate-crime coverage. National custody adds a conversion-therapy corrections policy and documented immigration-detention abuse reachable by a refused or detained visitor. Recourse is real but partial: national courts have enjoined several orders, employment and marriage protections stand, yet no documented remedy reaches facility exclusion or street violence, whose magnitude is unmeasurable (the killing figure is an undercount floor, so unused). Imprisonment is credible though not routine; no execution pathway.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable: document discrepancy or doubt about sex → refuse case; suspected misrepresentation → consider permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility; X-markers and non-birth-sex markers halted; Supreme Court let passport restrictions take effect Nov 2025; trans-athlete entry ban; travellers report passports confiscated/blocked abroad.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements, never automatic, with limited waiver; civil-liberties suit pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ published.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or fraud allegation → immigration custody, where trans detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2023 adult-entertainment statute criminalises 'male or female impersonators' anywhere a child could see (11m29d misdemeanour; 1–6yr felony on repeat), upheld, Supreme Court declined review. 2019 statute defines trans restroom use as indecent exposure. 2026 Act mandates birth-sex prison placement. National corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy policies (hair, hormones, drugs) from 2026.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; national employment statute covers firing; courts have enjoined several executive orders; 2021 sign mandate struck down 2022.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State arrest → birth-sex placement under state Act plus national conversion-therapy corrections policy; enforcement frequency of the drag and indecent-exposure statutes against trans visitors is not sourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: April 2026 Women's Safety and Protection Act: trans people must use birth-sex facilities; trans women barred from women's shelters. National executive order bars federally funded single-sex facility access by identity. National maps show facility bans across a majority of states, four with criminal triggers, six extending to private settings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some states and the capital district have no mapped ban; the 2021 small-business sign mandate was struck down; school-bathroom litigation is ongoing; no remedy shown operating for visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Every public restroom, shelter or ward the visitor enters is governed by the stricter of national and state rules; facility exclusion follows discovery regardless of local courtesy.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care banned (upheld by national Supreme Court June 2025), including out-of-state telehealth, with regret suits and $25,000 penalties; 2024 law adds civil penalties for adults helping a minor obtain care; inmate care banned; national funding freezes, crisis-lifeline LGBTQ service shut down, DOJ subpoenas of under-19 patient records.
care_services.protection: Not documented for adult visitors; emergency-care access for trans adults is not addressed in the dossier.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a minor who assists any transition-related step risks state civil penalties; care denial exposure for a detained or hospitalised visitor is an open question.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Dec 2025 DOJ reward memo listing 'radical gender ideology' among extreme viewpoints; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritising 'radically pro-transgender' groups alongside violent extremists; Jan 2025 order directing law enforcement to investigate schools and criminally prosecute teachers facilitating social transition; advocates compare the trajectory to early genocide stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The memo states the reward is not triggered by that phrase; the strategy says counterterrorism powers will not target those who merely disagree; several orders blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability that any outing escalates to state attention, compounding document and facility exposure.

minors_guardians.exposure: May 2024 state law requires teachers to report any child requesting a different name or pronoun to administrators and parents; care ban with penalties for assisting adults; sports restricted by birth sex with proof requirements; national order directing prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: National Justice Department legal challenge to the outing law is pending; national school-protection directive was enjoined in 2022 in one forum; several national orders litigated.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces the care ban, outing rules and civil penalties for assistance; a school-age minor in any facility hits birth-sex rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Gay/trans panic defence available to reduce punishment for fatal attacks; 2021 reporting describes police and legal officials turning a blind eye to assaults on LGBTQ people; reports of discrimination, refusal of service and beatings; state hate-crime statute omits gender identity; no statewide non-discrimination law.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Feb 2019 chief-prosecutor opinion allows sentencing enhancement for targeting a victim because transgender; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; national employment protection via 2020 Supreme Court ruling.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The 10-killings/18-years figure is an undercount floor and gives no usable magnitude; thin state recording (0/1/2 incidents) reflects practice, not incidence. Recourse depends on national statutes, since state coverage is absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide non-discrimination protection in employment, housing or public accommodations; municipal ordinances cover only public employment and are preempted for private employers; suit outcomes unsourced for the licence-marker case, the 2026 Act's facility provisions, the prison care ban and ongoing drag and school-bathroom litigation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning national courts have struck down the sign mandate, initially invalidated the drag law, and enjoined several executive orders; ACLU litigation and a legal-aid FAQ give a real, if slow, channel; marriage and employment protections stand.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy availability varies by stage: entry decisions and facility exclusion show no documented working remedy, while constitutional challenges demonstrably succeed sometimes.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's register excludes and humiliates but carries no imprisonment. This dossier is lower: an operative, upheld criminal statute targeting gender expression with up to a year's jail (felony on repeat), a birth-sex facility statute with an indecent-exposure charge attached, and a documented conversion-therapy corrections policy. Criminal custody exposure, not mere exclusion, is the operative worst case.

Kestrel Isles offers secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow appeals, with detention staying administrative. This dossier is materially lower: entry decisions can convert into a lifetime fraud finding and immigration custody with documented abuse, and the destination itself criminalises gender expression and mandates birth-sex facilities and prison placement.

Ostravia criminalises cross-dressing in administrative buildings, houses detainees by birth sex, arrests visitors, and offers only slow, principle-level remedies. This dossier matches that pattern (statewide drag ban, birth-sex custody and facilities, thin recourse) and adds a national custody regime applying conversion therapy; it sits only slightly higher because national courts, hate-crime and employment statutes do operate.

Drellia's universal registration exposure yields eviction and harassment but uncommon charges. This dossier is lower because criminal penalties attach to gender expression itself on public property, not merely to registration mismatch, and because custody placement by birth sex plus a conversion-therapy policy make detention severity greater.

parsed.synthesis: The visitor meets one system: entry rules that treat any document discrepancy as grounds for refusal and potentially a lifetime fraud finding, layered over a division that criminalises gender-expressive performance in public, requires birth-sex use of all covered facilities, charges trans restroom use as indecent exposure, and places detainees and shelter residents by birth sex. National custody converts any detention into exposure to a conversion-therapy corrections policy and, in immigration custody, documented abuse. Recourse is genuine but uneven: national courts block some measures, while no documented remedy reaches facility exclusion, entry decisions or street violence; state non-discrimination and gender-identity hate-crime coverage are absent, and police indifference is reported but dated. The violence figure is an undercount floor and is not used as magnitude. Net: criminal exposure credible but not routine, no execution pathway — High Risk, upper end.
